provisions.instrument: Ley General de Migración y Extranjería N.º 8764
Ley General de Migración y Extranjería N.º 8764

events.what_changed: Found that US deportees admitted on humanitarian grounds were not shown to have been told of the possibility of seeking refuge from their entry, and held the period of non-compliance injured their rights. This is a fact-specific finding with a 'take note' for future humanitarian admissions. It sets no general duty to advise before expulsion or rejection, so it is practice evidence only.
events.passage: No se demuestra; sin embargo, que tal información se transmitiera a las personas tuteladas desde el momento de su ingreso. [...] El lapso en el cual esta obligación se incumplió implicó la lesión de los derechos de las personas que eventualmente tuvieran acceso a la figura, de echar mano de ella [...] Tome nota la autoridad recurrida de lo dispuesto en esta sentencia a los efectos de eventuales autorizaciones de ingreso de personas por razones de humanidad.

answers.implementation_then_now: No protection on either date, so implementation does not apply. For the record: in 2025, HRW found that the entry order for the 200 US deportees did not mention asylum, and the Sala Constitucional found that the information was not given from the moment of entry. There is no evidence of a general information practice at either date.

answers.implementation_then_now: No protection on either date, so implementation does not apply. For context: in 2025, HRW and more than 40 NGOs criticised Costa Rica's role in the chain deportation of third-country nationals from the US.

practice_sources.title: Costa Rica: Allow Deported Migrants to Seek Asylum (Human Rights Watch)

answers.sourcing_note: The consolidated texts show no amendment notes on Ley 8764 arts. 31, 115 and 184 or regulation arts. 39 and 40. I did not re-read the version history of Constitution art. 31; it has had no known amendment.
answers.notes: No change. Art. 31(9) covers direct danger in any third country but not onward refoulement.

answers.change_2023_2026: There have been right protections both in 2023 and 2026 and neither the right protection nor the implementation level of these protections has changed

provisions.instrument: Ley General de Migración y Extranjería N.º 8764

events.what_changed: Partly upheld habeas corpus for about 200 US deportees held at CATEM-Sur without individual migration decisions and ordered individual status determinations. This is a finding on one group's facts, so it is practice evidence; the statutory rule is unchanged.
events.passage: La resolución D. JUR-0057-02-2025-JM, indicó que la permanencia podrá ser autorizada por una única vez y tendrá validez por un plazo de treinta días naturales, a efecto de que las personas beneficiadas puedan hacer abandono del país.

answers.implementation_then_now: In 2023 and 2026, DGME ordinarily decides deportation and expulsion by individual resolution, under review by the Sala Constitucional. The window contains one major documented breach: the February 2025 US-deportee group was held under a collective resolution rather than individual decisions. The Sala corrected this in June 2025, and the correction was slowly carried out (Defensoría, 2026). This is one episode, not a systemic shift, so the rating stays Usually on both dates. I read no practice evidence of the 2022-2023 period itself.

practice_sources.title: HRW, Costa Rica: Allow Deported Migrants to Seek Asylum

answers.sourcing_note: The consolidated Ley 8764 shows no amendment notes on the cited articles. Ley 10493 (2024) amended only arts. 33, 241 and 253. I could not open pre-2023 practice sources (the 2022 State Department report timed out and the UNHCR 2022 report returned a 404).
answers.notes: The 2023 implementation rating is carried over and not independently evidenced for its period.

provisions.instrument: Ley General de Migración y Extranjería N.º 8764

events.what_changed: Habeas corpus review of the detention and lack of information of the US deportee group. This is practice evidence that review of summary removals relies on the Sala; it does not change the statutory rules.
events.passage: El lapso en el cual esta obligación se incumplió implicó la lesión de los derechos de las personas que eventualmente tuvieran acceso a la figura, de echar mano de ella, por lo que también este extremo del recurso debe estimarse.

answers.implementation_then_now: On both dates, the expulsion of lawful residents has evidence and suspensive appeal stages, while the deportation of irregular migrants is summary with no administrative appeal (art. 222). In practice, review depends on habeas corpus. The 2025 US-deportee episode, found unlawful by the Sala, illustrates the gap but is not a shift in the overall level. I read no practice evidence from the 2022-2023 period.
